methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly combat concentration by building grassroots capability outside traditional tech hubs, signaling potential for peer-driven distributed fluency if this model scales beyond individual efforts.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's formal partnership with AI Ready RVA creates institutional infrastructure for deep AI capability but remains anchored to a metro region, potentially widening the gap with rural areas lacking similar university-community AI partnerships.

signals.title: Tech Briefs: New bill backed by Warner would curb energy costs, demands from data centers
signals.signal_reading: While ARC funding for Radford's AI workforce study shows concern for rural areas, it remains at the research phase rather than deployment, highlighting how underserved regions get studies while metros get data centers and implementation.

signals.title: University of Mary Washington Adds Virginia’s First Master’s Degree in AI in Business - Northern Virginia Magazine
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's first AI business master's degree at UMW concentrates advanced credential-building in educated populations with graduate school access, deepening rather than distributing specialized AI capability across the workforce spectrum.

signals.title: VA’s OIT Staff Saving 8 Hours a Week With AI, Official Says - MeriTalk
signals.signal_reading: State IT staff saving 8 hours weekly with AI tools demonstrates shallow but effective platform-based adoption that could distribute productivity gains broadly if replicated across government agencies statewide, though without building deep technical capability.
